summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, morbid obesity, chronic diastolic heart failure, obstructive sleep apnea, and a history of venous thrombosis was admitted for surgical management of a right breast mass. She had a history of an enlarging breast lesion concerning for cancer, with recent imaging showing growth from 9mm to 14mm. Preoperatively, she was bridged from warfarin to heparin due to her anticoagulation needs. She underwent ultrasound-guided wire localization followed by a wire-localized right partial mastectomy with global re-excision. The procedure was successful, with final pathology revealing multifocal invasive ductal carcinoma, 0.6cm and 1.2cm, with clear margins. She tolerated the surgery well, remained on her home medications adjusted for dialysis, and completed two hemodialysis sessions during admission. The drain was removed on hospital day 5, and she was discharged home with plans for surgical and oncology follow-up, ongoing dialysis, and continuation of her chronic disease management.
problems: Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage V or end stage renal disease
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
